title: Set the price cap

predict.q: A natural monopoly sells 180 units at its own price of 22. A regulator sets a price cap of 16. What happens?

options.s: Output stays at 180; only profit falls.
options.fb: Under the cap each extra unit adds the capped price (16) to revenue, which is above MC (4). So the firm sells more, up to the demand curve: Q = 240.

options.s: Output rises to 240; profit falls but stays above normal.
options.fb: At 16 the firm sells 240 along the demand curve. AC is 11.5, so profit is 1,080: lower, but still above normal.

options.s: Output falls, because the firm earns less on each unit.
options.fb: A price ceiling cuts quantity in a competitive market, not here. The capped monopolist no longer has to cut its price to sell more, so it raises output.

options.s: Output rises to 240, and the firm makes a loss.
options.fb: At Q = 240, AC is 11.5, below the cap of 16: profit is 1,080. A loss starts only when the cap is below P = AC (10).

task: Move the price-cap slider from 22 down to 4 and watch output, AC and profit.

target.do: Set the price cap to 16, then press Check.

takeaway: Lowering the cap raises output; profit is normal at P = AC (10); below that the firm makes a loss.
